verdict.rationale: Stripe documents a first-party catalog publishing path for sellers. Merchants format a CSV product/variant feed and upload it through the v2 Product Catalog Import API to a presigned URL, with documented cadence, replace-mode deletion semantics, import-status webhooks with per-row error CSVs, and required restricted-key permissions; the stated purpose is sharing product, price, and availability with agents. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the import flow, coverage of service catalogs (ACS states it supports purchases of physical goods), and general availability (the agent-side feed ingestion is private preview and gated by per-agent approval).

support.subject: As a merchant, I can publish my product or service catalog into agent surfaces through a documented feed or import API so AI agents can discover what I sell

citations.quote: Format your feed as a CSV where each row is a product or variant
It lets you share product, price, and availability information with agents while minimizing changes to your existing commerce systems.
the full checkout lifecycle through Stripe, including product feed ingestion, cart management, fulfillment, and payment collection
